= Working With ExportStats =
The JSON format provided by ExportStats is a rudimentary but solid source for a lot of in-game data, although the structure is currently undocumented. Working with the devs directly has allowed us to compile a list of what each part of the JSON is mapped to. For an overview of the shape, a sample export has been uploaded to [[/example.json]]

== The array structure ==
The JSON object copied to the user's clipboard is a JSON block with the following top level elements.
{| class="wikitable mw-code"
|+ Top Level Array Elements
! Field ||  Type || Description || Example
|-id="version"
| <syntaxhighlight lang="json" inline>"version"</syntaxhighlight>
! <syntaxhighlight lang="gdscript" inline>string</syntaxhighlight>
| The version of the game the export is from. Use this to compare if their export is compatible with your sheet, i.e. may be lacking critical information, or warn them that they may have new sources of gains that is not accounted for in your project.
| <syntaxhighlight lang="pycon">
>>> json["version"]
"v2.2.21"</syntaxhighlight>
|-id="time"
| <syntaxhighlight lang="json" inline>"time"</syntaxhighlight>
! <syntaxhighlight lang="gdscript" inline>number</syntaxhighlight>
| The time that the export was performed at.
| <syntaxhighlight lang="pycon">>>> x = json.time
>>> print(x)
46259.86238
>>> print(datetime(1899, 12, 30) + timedelta(days=x))
2026-09-13 20:41:53</syntaxhighlight>
<ref>I blame Julk for this. Not the game maker export, Unix time as a concept.</ref>
|-id="stats"
| <syntaxhighlight lang="json" inline>"stats"</syntaxhighlight>
! <syntaxhighlight lang="gdscript" inline>Array<JSON></syntaxhighlight>
| The nested stats objects.
| <syntaxhighlight lang="pycon">
>>> x = json["stats"]
>>> len(x)
420</syntaxhighlight>
|}

=== Time formatting ===
Language-specific implementation of how to parse the time format is beyond the scope of this Guide, however, for Google Sheets, formatting a cell to Number -> Date Time will display it as a Date and Time directly, alternatively can be used by having it in a cell and using the following snippet.
<syntaxhighlight lang="scilab" copy>=LET(
   t, VALUE(TRIM(<Cell Reference>)),
   delta, NOW()-t,
   days, INT(delta),
   hours, INT(MOD(delta, 1)*24),
   minutes, INT(MOD(delta*1440,60)),
   seconds, ROUND(MOD(delta * 86400, 60)),
  days & "d" & hours & "h" & minutes & "m" & seconds & "s ago")
</syntaxhighlight>
which produces this output <code style="color:green">0d12h6m15s ago</code>

=== Extracting the Stats ===
For most languages, JSON can be mapped easily using standard dot bracket notation, either as a property accessor or key value pairing, i.e. <syntaxhighlight lang="python" inline>Json.stats</syntaxhighlight> or <syntaxhighlight lang="pycon" inline>Json["stats"]</syntaxhighlight>. If you're unfamiliar with that format, I'm surprised you're even this far through. For Google Sheets or excel, there isn't a nice easy way to import the JSON, generally users are expected to paste down a range, alternatively I created this snippet which can be pointed at a cell to spread the data into a 2-Column Wide Key Value pairing list. <code style="color:pink">JSON</code> is a named 1 cell range in the below example.
<syntaxhighlight lang="scilab" copy>=let(
  txt, regexreplace(JSON, """[^""]+""\s*:\s*\[[^\]]*\]\s*,?", ""),
  raw, split(txt, ",{}", true),
  key_val, arrayformula(split(transpose(raw), ":")),
  noquotes, lambda(x, substitute(x, char(34), "")),
  capitalise, lambda(x, let(ch, left(x, 1), replace(x, 1, 1, upper(ch)))),
  fmt, lambda(x, capitalise(noquotes(trim(x)))),
  keys, arrayformula(fmt(index(key_val,,1))),
  values, arrayformula(trim(index(key_val,,2))),
  parsed, arrayformula(
  if(values="",, 
  if(values="true", true, 
  if(values="false", false, 
  if(left(values)=char(34), noquotes(values), 
  value(values)))))),
  sort(filter(hstack(keys, parsed), keys<>"")))
</syntaxhighlight>

From there, you can more readily access the data you are looking for using <syntaxhighlight lang="scilab" inline copy>=xlookup("stat_name", B1:B, C1:C)</syntaxhighlight>

== Stats Items ==
Within the JSON, fields come under three main types. Singletons, Arrays, and pseudo-arrays-as-singletons within the base structure. The majority of the fields are direct 1:1 exports of of in-game "Stat" listings, however there are also some meta-status fields listed below.
{| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center"
|+ Meta-progression Items
|-
! colspan="2" | Field !! Type !! Details !! Example
|- id="obelisk_level"
| [[File:Obelisk_Level_12_Icon.png|20x20px]] 
! <syntaxhighlight lang="json" inline>"obelisk_level"</syntaxhighlight>
| <syntaxhighlight lang="gdscript" inline>number</syntaxhighlight> 
| The Obelisk Level the player has reached.
| rowspan=5 style="text-align:left" | <syntaxhighlight lang="pycon">>>> print(json["stats"]["obelisk_level"])
70</syntaxhighlight>
|- id="blackhole"
| [[File:BlackHole.png|20x20px]] 
! <syntaxhighlight lang="json" inline>"black_hole_level"</syntaxhighlight>
| <syntaxhighlight lang="gdscript" inline>integer</syntaxhighlight> 
|The Black Hole Level the player has reached.
|- id="current_floor"
| [[File:Misc_Floor_73.png|20x20px]] 
! <syntaxhighlight lang="json" inline>"current_floor"</syntaxhighlight>
| <syntaxhighlight lang="gdscript" inline>number</syntaxhighlight> 
|The current floor the player was on when they exported their stats, useful for checking if is a -Game Speed floor or similar.
|- id="worlds_unlocked"
| [[File:World_2_monument.png|20x20px]] 
! <syntaxhighlight lang="json" inline>"worlds_unlocked"</syntaxhighlight>
| <syntaxhighlight lang="gdscript" inline>number</syntaxhighlight> 
| The number of worlds the player has unlocked.
|-
| [[File:World_4_monument.png|20x20px]] 
! <syntaxhighlight lang="json" inline>"world_4_quest_progress"</syntaxhighlight>
| <syntaxhighlight lang="gdscript" inline>integer</syntaxhighlight>
| Number of World 4 Quests completed.
|}

== Pseudo-Arrays ==

=== Veins ===
Vein unlock research and the 2x vein spawn rate research are handled by a single variable each. If the number is greater than or equal to the vein index, it is researched (or 2x is researched).

True</syntaxhighlight>

=== Construct ===
Some of the earlier objects in the export are the construct arrays, They are mapped by World and Statue Position to a value from 0 - 3, representing the following states

{| class="wikitable mw-code"  style="text-align: center;"
|+ Constructed Statue Values
|-
! Value 
|| <syntaxhighlight lang="json" inline>0.0</syntaxhighlight> || <syntaxhighlight lang="json" inline>1.0</syntaxhighlight> || <syntaxhighlight lang="json" inline>2.0</syntaxhighlight> || <syntaxhighlight lang="json" inline>3.0....</syntaxhighlight>
|-
! State
|| Not Built || Built || Gilded || Platinised
|}
<tabbertransclude>
Guides/Working_With_ExportStats/World1Statues|World 1
Guides/Working_With_ExportStats/World3Statues|World 3
Guides/Working_With_ExportStats/World4Statues|World 4
</tabbertransclude>
